steps.say: The mean shares the total out equally. Add all the values, then divide by how many there are.

figure.title: Books read
figure.alt: A bar chart of books read: Aisha 6, Budi 9, Citra 4 and Dimas 5.

steps.say: The mean of 6, 9, 4 and 5 is 6. If they all read the same number of books, each would read 6.
The median is the middle value in order. With an even number of values, find halfway between the middle two.
The mode is the most common value. The range is the biggest value minus the smallest.
To compare two sets of data, use an average and the range. A smaller range means the values are more consistent.

check.prompt: Hana scored 8, 9, 10, 9 and 9 points in 5 games. Ben scored 2, 15, 9, 6 and 13. Who is more consistent?
hints: Consistent means the scores stay close together.
Find the range for each player.
Hana's highest score is 10 and her lowest is 8.
check.explanation: Both have a mean of 9, but Hana's range is 2 and Ben's range is 13. Hana is more consistent.

options.text: Ben, because his range is bigger
options.why: A bigger range means the scores are more spread out.
One high score does not make a player consistent.

options.why: The means are equal, but the ranges are very different.
